question: A police car detects a stolen vehicle 1 km in front of it and begins to pursue it. The police car is moving at a speed of 100 km/h, while the stolen car is traveling at 80 km/h. What will be the distance between them after 90 seconds?
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**Relative speed** = 100 − 80 = 20 km/h.

Gap reduced in 90 seconds = 20 × (5/18) × 90 = 500 m.

Initial gap = 1 km = 1000 m.

Distance after 90 seconds = 1000 − 500 = 500 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 500 m.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Initial distance = 1 km = 1000 m, **Police speed** = 100 km/h, **Stolen car speed** = 80 km/h, Time = 90 seconds.

**Formula Used:** Relative Speed (same direction) = u − v; Distance = Speed × Time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7c7a839635b6fff0971912df3a14d368438d30fb79d3a1dd0d6ac05b4a5055ac.png] 

⇒ **Relative Speed** = 100 − 80 = 20 km/h

⇒ Speed in m/s = 20 × (5/18) = 50/9 m/s

⇒ Distance covered in 90 seconds = (50/9) × 90 = 500 m

⇒ **Final distance** between them = 1000 − 500 = 500 m

**∴ The correct answer is 500 m.**

**__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed Concept

When two objects move in the **same direction**, relative speed is the difference (u − v). In **opposite directions**, it is the sum (u + v).

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from **km/h to m/s**, multiply by 5/18. To convert **m/s to km/h**, multiply by 18/5.

Catching Time

The time taken to catch an object is calculated as: **Time** = Initial Distance ÷ Relative Speed.</p
